articles.title: The US Has Run Out of EB-2 Green Cards for Indians This Year. No More Approvals Until October.
articles.excerpt: The State Department confirmed that all EB-2 immigrant visa numbers for India-born applicants have been exhausted for FY2026, freezing final residency approvals for thousands of skilled professionals.
articles.nri_angle: The EB-2 freeze directly affects hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals in the US on H-1B visas waiting for permanent residency.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Economy Grew Just 1.6 Percent Last Quarter. That Is Worse Than Anyone Expected.
articles.excerpt: A sharp downward revision to first-quarter GDP, driven by weaker consumer spending and the Iran war's inflationary toll, signals trouble ahead for hiring, mortgages, and the Indian professionals who depend on both.
articles.nri_angle: A slowing US economy directly impacts the 4.8 million Indian-origin Americans through hiring freezes, H-1B sponsorship pullbacks, higher mortgage rates, reduced remittance purchasing power, and a political environment less receptive to immigration reform. India received $129B in remittances in FY2025 — any US economic slowdown ripples directly to families back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seventy Percent of Karachi Has No Reliable Water. India's Indus Treaty Suspension Is Only Part of the Story.
articles.excerpt: Pakistan's financial capital faces a severe water crisis as the Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance. But the real causes run deeper than geopolitics.
articles.nri_angle: The Indus Waters Treaty was a cornerstone of India-Pakistan relations that the diaspora followed closely. Its suspension signals a new phase in India's strategic posture, while the Karachi crisis exposes how infrastructure failures — not just geopolitics — drive water scarcity in the subcontinent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Quad Just Agreed to Build a Port in Fiji and Launch a Critical Minerals Pact. India Hosted It All.
articles.excerpt: The 11th Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi produced the grouping's first joint infrastructure project, a framework for critical minerals supply chains, and a maritime surveillance system — signalling the alliance is moving past photo-ops into operational territory.
articles.nri_angle: The Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework directly benefits Indian tech and manufacturing supply chains. For NRIs in tech and defence industries, alternative supply chains away from China reduce geopolitical risk. The energy security initiative addresses the Hormuz disruption that has raised fuel costs affecting remittance value and Indian market returns.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Called the NEET Paper Leak 'Very Traumatic.' The Government Said Modi Is Personally Supervising.
articles.excerpt: Justices Narasimha and Aradhe told the NTA to learn from the UPSC, the CBI is probing a Maharashtra conspiracy ring, and a retest is set for June 21 — the second NEET cancellation in three years.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian families abroad who send their children to take NEET for medical college admissions in India, the disruption is acutely painful. Many candidates travel to India specifically for the exam, arranging accommodation, coaching, and leave. A cancellation followed by a retest weeks later imposes enormous logistical and emotional costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The UAE Secretly Struck Iran Dozens of Times During the War. 3.5 Million Indians Live There.
articles.excerpt: A Wall Street Journal investigation reveals the Emirates carried out coordinated strikes on Iranian targets from the war's earliest days through the ceasefire — a far deeper military role than Gulf nations publicly acknowledged, with direct implications for the region's largest expatriate community.
articles.nri_angle: An estimated 3.5 million Indians live and work in the UAE — the largest Indian expatriate community in any single country. The revelation that the UAE was an active combatant, not a neutral bystander, directly affects the security calculus for Indian professionals and families who remained in the country throughout the conflict.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is Down to the Last 1 Percent. A Delegation Arrives in Delhi Next Week.
articles.excerpt: Ambassador Sergio Gor says the deal could be signed within weeks. But the 'last 1 percent' is the hardest part — and the legal landscape under it has shifted.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chandrayaan-3 Has Won America's Highest Honor in Astronautics. ISRO Joins Jeff Bezos on the List.
articles.excerpt: The AIAA Goddard Astronautics Award recognizes the 2023 moon landing that made India the first nation to reach the lunar south pole. India's ambassador accepted it in Washington.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Signed a $629 Million BrahMos Missile Deal With Vietnam. Indonesia Is Next.
articles.excerpt: The defence secretary confirmed the deal at the Shangri-La Dialogue — making Vietnam India's second export customer for the supersonic cruise missile after the Philippines.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Dropped Criminal Charges Against Gautam Adani. His Stock Surged 22% in a Month.
articles.excerpt: The DOJ moved to dismiss the bribery case. The SEC settled for $18 million. Adani Enterprises paid $275 million to resolve Iran sanctions allegations. The legal cloud that once wiped $150 billion off the Adani empire is lifting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vinesh Phogat's Comeback Ends in the Semifinals. The Supreme Court Could Not Save Her on the Mat.
articles.excerpt: A day after the Supreme Court intervened to let her compete, the Olympic wrestler lost 4-6 to Meenakshi Goyat in the Asian Games selection trials. Her dream of Aichi-Nagoya is over.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Last Maoist Rebels Are Surrendering. A CNN Investigation Went to the Jungle to Watch.
articles.excerpt: Papa Rao emerged from the forests of Chhattisgarh with a $26,000 bounty on his head and 17 comrades in tow. After nearly six decades, India's Naxal insurgency is in its death throes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Finance Ministry Has Named the Single Biggest Risk to the Economy. It Is the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.excerpt: The ministry's monthly economic report warns that fuel price hikes, a weak monsoon, and the Middle East conflict will push retail inflation higher in the coming months.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee Was Pelted With Eggs, Stones, and Shoes in Sonarpur. He Wore a Cricket Helmet.
articles.excerpt: The TMC general secretary visited families of party workers killed in post-poll violence. Protesters with black flags, eggs, and bricks met him at every stop.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CUET-UG 2026 Delayed Across India After TCS Technical Glitch. The Timing Could Not Be Worse.
articles.excerpt: The Common University Entrance Test was delayed by two hours at centres in Delhi, Noida, Bangalore, and Varanasi — the fourth national exam controversy in two months.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SEBI Has Finally Cleared NDTV of Disclosure Violations. The Case Began in 2009.
articles.excerpt: India's markets regulator ruled that no change of control occurred under a 2009 loan agreement — ending a 17-year-old saga for the Adani-owned broadcaster.

sources.label: Securities and Exchange Board of India

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single Day of Extreme Heat Kills 3,400 People Across India. A New Study Finally Counted.
articles.excerpt: UC Berkeley researchers found that a five-day heatwave causes nearly 30,000 excess deaths — and India is heading into its worst monsoon in 11 years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Has Skipped the Shangri-La Dialogue for Two Years in a Row. The Rest of Asia Noticed.
articles.excerpt: Beijing sent a low-profile delegation of PLA academics while India held five bilateral defence meetings and the US, UK, and Australia announced a new undersea drone programme.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Weeklong Standoff at a Newark Detention Center Is Rewriting the Rules of Immigration Enforcement. Legal Immigrants Are Watching.
articles.excerpt: New Jersey's governor ordered state police to create protest zones outside Delaney Hall as dueling demonstrations, pepper spray, and an FBI arrest intensified the confrontation
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Allows Vinesh Phogat to Compete in Asian Games Trials. Then It Warned Courts to Stay Out of Sports.
articles.excerpt: The apex court cleared the wrestler for selection trials beginning May 30 but delivered a pointed rebuke about judicial overreach in sporting events
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: SEBI Has Fined Suzlon Energy ₹15.95 Crore for Inflating Its Books. The Chairman and Vice-Chairman Got Personal Penalties Too.
articles.excerpt: The markets regulator said Suzlon's disclosures 'created a false picture of financial strength' and misled investors through transactions with subsidiaries
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Defence Secretary Held Five Bilateral Meetings in One Day at Shangri-La. Here Is What Each One Was About.
articles.excerpt: Rajesh Kumar Singh met counterparts from the Netherlands, Australia, the EU, and key Indo-Pacific partners on the sidelines of Asia's biggest defense forum
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Sensex Fell 850 Points in 10 Minutes on Friday. The Explanation That Went Viral Was Wrong.
articles.excerpt: India's weight in the MSCI index barely moved — from 12.4% to 12.3%. But social media said MSCI had dumped India, and Rs 6 lakh crore vanished before anyone checked.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Myanmar's Junta Leader Just Chose India for His First Trip as President. The Real Prize Is Under the Ground.
articles.excerpt: Min Aung Hlaing's five-day visit to New Delhi is less about diplomacy and more about rare earths, border security, and keeping China from getting everything.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Federal Judge Just Asked Whether There Is Any Limit to the $100,000 H-1B Fee. The Government Had No Clear Answer.
articles.excerpt: U.S. District Judge Leo Sorokin questioned whether the president's power to deter foreign workers has any boundary. Only 85 employers have paid the fee since September.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court Overturns ₹447 Crore Fraud Order Against Reliance. SEBI Must Return ₹250 Crore.
articles.excerpt: India's apex court ruled that breaching position limits is not the same as committing fraud — a distinction that could reshape how SEBI pursues market manipulation cases for years to come.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Texas Can Now Arrest and Deport People Suspected of Crossing Illegally. The Law Is in Effect as of Friday.
articles.excerpt: A federal appeals court lifted an injunction against SB4, a law that makes unauthorized border crossing a state crime and lets Texas judges — not federal ones — issue deportation orders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Fed Is Now Openly Talking About Raising Interest Rates. NRIs With American Mortgages Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Multiple Federal Reserve officials said on Friday they may need to hike rates if the Iran war keeps pushing inflation higher. The PCE index just hit 3.8 percent.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pentagon Chief Praises India's Military Readiness at Shangri-La. Then He Told Asian Allies to Spend 3.5% of GDP on Defense.
articles.excerpt: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth singled out India as a partner that is 'improving military readiness' — while warning that freeloading allies will be pushed to the back of the line.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Analysts Just Raised Oil Forecasts for the Third Time Since the Iran War Began. India Cannot Afford This.
articles.excerpt: Brent crude is now forecast to average $90.44 per barrel in 2026 — up 40% from pre-war estimates. For India, the world's third-largest oil importer, every dollar of that increase bleeds into inflation, the trade deficit, and the rupee.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Piyush Goyal Just Finished a 10-Day Sprint Across North America. Here's What He Got Done.
articles.excerpt: The Commerce Minister met CEOs at Morgan Stanley, Mastercard, and Warburg Pincus in New York, pushed a $50 billion trade target in Canada, and confirmed a US delegation is coming to Delhi next week for BTA talks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Made $17.7 Billion Selling Dollars to Defend the Rupee. Then It Gave a Record $30 Billion to the Government.
articles.excerpt: The central bank's annual report shows foreign exchange gains rose 52%, its balance sheet topped $961 billion, and it transferred a record ₹2.87 trillion to the federal government — the largest such payout in RBI history.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Forecast Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years. El Niño Is Coming.
articles.excerpt: The IMD now projects rainfall at just 90% of the long-period average — the lowest since 2015. With oil prices already elevated and inflation creeping up, a failed monsoon could push food prices into crisis territory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: AAP Just Swept Punjab's Municipal Elections. Congress Finished Second. The BJP Barely Registered.
articles.excerpt: The results from Mohali, Ludhiana, and other civic bodies confirm that Bhagwant Mann's party has consolidated its hold on Punjab. For NRIs with property and family in the state, AAP's dominance in local government means their dealings with Punjab bureaucracy now go through one party.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York's First South Asian Mayor Will Skip the Israel Day Parade. The Political Cost Could Be Enormous.
articles.excerpt: Zohran Mamdani's decision to boycott the parade puts him at odds with New York's political establishment. For South Asian Americans navigating US politics, his stance on Israel is either principled leadership or political self-destruction.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: VFS Global Staff Say They Have 'Sales Targets' for Services That Are Supposed to Be Optional
articles.excerpt: An investigation across 20 countries found that VFS centres in Delhi and Mumbai routinely pressure visa applicants into paying for premium services. For NRIs helping family members apply for Schengen visas, this confirms what they already suspected.

sources.label: The Indian Express via Press Post

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'Learn From UPSC': Supreme Court Rips Into NTA Over the Second NEET Paper Leak in Two Years
articles.excerpt: The court says the agency's ad-hoc structure is the root cause. For Indian American families who spend lakhs on NEET coaching, the message is clear: the system that decides their children's futures cannot be trusted to secure its own exams.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Siddaramaiah Has Resigned as Karnataka Chief Minister. DK Shivakumar Will Take His Place.
articles.excerpt: After three years of power-sharing tension, Congress finally hands the state to its organizational strongman. For Kannadigas in the diaspora, the leadership change could reshape how the party approaches overseas voter engagement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The RBI Just Revealed Plans to Let NRIs Send Money Home Through the Digital Rupee
articles.excerpt: India's central bank has signed pacts with Singapore and the UAE to pilot cross-border digital rupee payments — a move that could eliminate the fees and delays that cost the diaspora billions every year.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Just Ruled That Google Cannot Sell Your Brand Name to Your Competitors
articles.excerpt: The Hindware judgment strips Google of safe harbour protection and establishes that auctioning trademarks as ad keywords constitutes infringement — a ruling that Indian founders from Zerodha to Shaadi.com are calling a turning point.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Absolut Vodka and Chivas Regal Are Banned in Delhi. The Court Just Said They Will Stay Banned.
articles.excerpt: Delhi High Court rejected Pernod Ricard's plea to resume sales in the capital, extending a three-year exile rooted in a liquor policy investigation where charges have never been framed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Day in Two Months. The Reason: Oil Fell and the RBI Stepped In.
articles.excerpt: India's currency jumped 0.7 percent to 95 per dollar as Iran deal hopes collided with central bank intervention. But $24 billion has already left since March.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Intel Just Signed a $3.3 Billion Deal to Build a Semiconductor Plant in Odisha. This Is Not a Promise. It Is an MoU.
articles.excerpt: The facility will make glass-core substrates for AI and 5G chips. It is the biggest single-site semiconductor investment India has ever landed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The WHO Just Named the Three Drugs and Two Vaccines That Could Stop Ebola. One Vaccine Is From India.
articles.excerpt: With 906 suspected cases and 223 deaths, the WHO has fast-tracked experimental treatments for the Bundibugyo strain. The Oxford-Serum Institute vaccine could be ready for trials in two months.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satellite Images Show China Building 80 Launch Pads Near Its Nuclear Silos. India Should Be Paying Attention.
articles.excerpt: A Reuters investigation reveals a sprawling military complex in Xinjiang designed to ensure China can strike back after a nuclear attack. The implications reach far beyond the US-China rivalry.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Trump Is in the Situation Room Deciding on Iran. India, Which Imports 90 Percent of Its Oil, Is Watching.
articles.excerpt: A 60-day ceasefire extension could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease India's $102-a-barrel crude crisis. But analysts warn the relief may be temporary.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 142,000 Tech Jobs Have Been Cut in 2026. For Indian H-1B Workers, Every Layoff Is a Deportation Clock.
articles.excerpt: AI is replacing junior developers at scale, companies are hiring in Bangalore instead of Boston, and H-1B holders who lose their jobs have 60 days before they must leave the country. The American tech dream is fracturing along visa lines.
articles.image_caption: Indian tech professionals on H-1B visas face a unique double bind: lose your job, and the clock starts ticking on your legal right to stay in the country.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Still Has No Broadcaster for the FIFA World Cup. The Tournament Starts in 13 Days.
articles.excerpt: FIFA initially wanted $100 million for India's broadcast rights. Nobody paid. Now Zee Entertainment is in last-minute talks, an Indian American firm claims it won a secret bid, and a Delhi court is demanding free-to-air coverage. A billion fans are waiting.
articles.image_caption: The 2026 FIFA World Cup begins June 11, but India's 1.4 billion people still do not have a confirmed broadcaster.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The U.S. Just Threatened to Shut Down International Flights at Newark. The FIFA World Cup Starts in 13 Days.
articles.excerpt: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin says customs officers could be pulled from sanctuary city airports, stranding millions of travelers — including the diaspora — weeks before the World Cup kicks off in New Jersey.
articles.image_caption: Newark Liberty International Airport, a major gateway for international travelers and the Indian diaspora on the U.S. East Coast.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and South Korea Just Signed a Defense and Cyber Pact in Seoul. The Indo-Pacific Chessboard Is Getting More Crowded.
articles.excerpt: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's visit produced an MoU on military cyber security, defence information sharing, and joint technology development — deepening a 'Special Strategic Partnership' that both sides are now treating as a pillar of Indo-Pacific stability.
articles.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh signed the new MoU with his South Korean counterpart Ahn Gyu-back in Seoul
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
